summary: Jean Kellens works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Liège (~1961–1966) and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1966–1972), later holding posts at Mainz (~1974–1993), Liège (~1993–1994), and Collège de France (1993).
Specializing in philosophy and linguistics, Jean Petitot studied at the École polytechnique (~1963–1965). He later served there as director from circa 1999 to 2006.

Indologist and archaeologist Jean Philippe Vogel studied at the University of Amsterdam under J. H. C. Kern and C. C. Uhlenbeck. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as director at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss at EPHE. He held professorships at INALCO (1913–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot worked in Indology and other fields, studying at École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace. His main academic posts included professorships at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige specialized in archaeology and Indology, studying at École du Louvre and the University of Paris. He served as director and head of the Musée Guimet from 1986 to 2004 and circa 1986 to 2008.

Philosopher Jean-François Lyotard studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at Paris Nanterre (1967–1970), Paris 1 (1970–1972), Paris 8 (1972–1987), UC Irvine (~1987–1993), and Emory University (~1993–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say (~1937–1941), Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at Collège Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826), the University of Paris (~1808–1844), and as chair of Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the CNRS (attested 2003–2004).
Jean-Luc Chevillard specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli (~1985–1990), and he became a researcher at the CNRS circa 1992.

Jean-Noël Robert specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology, having studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held positions at EPHE (from 1979), CNRS (1975–1990), and the Collège de France as director (2010–2022).

Sinologist and linguist Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator and president at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1824, 1832).

Jean-Pierre Drège works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy Europe, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet (~1970–1976), and served as president of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

Indologist and art historian Jeannine Auboyer studied under Hackin, Grousset, Przyluski, and others at EPHE and École du Louvre. She held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1980) and served as chief curator at Musée Guimet (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven studied at Worcester College, Oxford, and Yale University. He was a junior fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows (~1996–1999) and became a professor of English at Princeton University circa 1999.

Philosopher Jeff Malpas studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He headed the philosophy programme at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) before serving as professor and emeritus distinguished professor at the University of Tasmania (1999, 2018).
Jeff Watt specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and art history/archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, studying under mentor Taitetsu Unno and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago Divinity School, taking up a post at Elizabethtown College in 2000.
